item.title: Counting elliptic curves by discriminant
item.description: arXiv:2611.31390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula with a power saving for the number of $\mathbb{Q}$-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves $E/\mathbb{Q}$ ordered by minimal discriminant, assuming the $abc$ conjecture. Unconditionally, we obtain the same asymptotic for the curves with $|\Delta_{\min}(E)| \le X$ and $c_4(E) \le X^{8/3 - \delta}$ for any fixed $\delta > 0$, by obtaining new bounds for the number of integral points $(c_4, c_6)$ near the cusp $c_4^3 = c_6^2$.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Chan, Peter Koymans

item.title: Matrix Criteria for Mordell--Weil Ranks of Quartic Twists of $y^2=x^3+x$ with Root Number $-1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.31473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Mordell--Weil ranks of quartic twists $E_a:y^2=x^3+ax$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with global root number $-1$. For $D$ a product of $n\ge2$ distinct odd primes, a $2$-isogeny descent yields unconditional rank bounds for $E_D$, $E_{-D}$, and $E_{-2D}$ in terms of matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ defined by additive Legendre symbols. Under suitable congruence and matrix-rank conditions, these curves have rank at most one, and rank one assuming the Mordell--Weil parity conjecture. For $E_{-2D}$, an additional explicit square condition establishes rank one unconditionally. Our results extend earlier two-prime criteria to arbitrary numbers of prime factors and further to fourth-power-free coefficients $H=\prod_{i=1}^n\ell_i^{e_i}$, where $e_i\in\{1,3\}$.
item.dc:creator: Debajyoti De

item.title: Irrationality and differential equations: the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang
item.description: arXiv:2611.31507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Beautiful recent work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang has given new methods for proving irrationality of certain arithmetically interesting constants, notably $L(2, \chi_{-3})$, building on ideas of Siegel, Andr\'e, Bost-Charles, and others. This note is meant to explain some of this work for the 2027 JMM Current Events Bulletin, and to situate it in context of some results and conjectures in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Litt

item.title: Smale's Mean Values And Geometric Mean Values
item.description: arXiv:2611.31546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for every integer $d>2$ and every $L>0$, there exists a polynomial of degree $d$ whose geometric mean value exceeds $L$. This result demonstrates that the geometric mean value alone is insufficient to establish the smallest upper bound for the minimum of Smale's mean values. Under certain additional assumptions, we derive upper bounds for the geometric mean value, thereby verifying Smale's mean value conjecture for several subclasses of polynomials. Furthermore, we connect Smale's mean values to Fekete points. Motivated by this connection, we formulate a new problem concerning Fekete points in the spirit of Smale's mean values.
item.dc:creator: Yunping Jiang, Zhe Wang

item.title: On the leading constant in Manin's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.31562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We disprove a conjecture of Batyrev and Tschinkel concerning counting rational points of bounded height. Our results strongly suggest that the transcendental Brauer group plays a role in the leading constant in problems of the same nature such as the Manin--Peyre conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Chan, Peter Koymans, Nick Rome, Tim Santens

item.title: The Residual Unitary Case for Almost Elusive Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.31657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this short note, we remove the residual unitary family in Hall's classification of almost elusive classical groups and the corresponding conditional family in the quasiprimitive classification. Using theorems of Zsigmondy and Schinzel together with some elementary number theory arguments, we prove that if n > 4 is odd, f > 1 is even, and r is the unique primitive prime divisor of (2^f)^{2n} - 1, then 4nf divides r - 1. For n > 4 prime and any positive integer f, we deduce that a unique primitive prime divisor r of (2^f)^{2n} - 1 satisfies r > 4nf, except when (n, f, r) = (5, 1, 11). We then obtain two conjugacy classes of derangements of the same prime order in a broader family of unitary subspace actions, and a quadratic lower bound for the number of such classes in the corresponding product actions.
item.dc:creator: Alan Xuelun Hou, Tudor Popescu

item.title: Generalized Tate--Nakayama duality for complexes of tori over local function fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.31675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define the cohomology set $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$ for a complex $Z \to T \to U$ with $T$, $U$ tori over a local function field $F$ and $Z$ a finite subgroup of $T$, where $\mathcal{E}$ is the gerbe from [Dil23]. We follow the method of [Kal26] and prove that the Tate--Nakayama isomorphism [Dil23, Theorem 4.10] for $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T)$ extends to $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$, which lets one generalize Kaletha's parametrization [Kal21] of supercuspidal $L$-packets to local function fields.
item.dc:creator: Peter Dillery

item.title: Counting solutions to Euclidean Fermat equations
item.dc:creator: Niven T. Achenjang, Santiago Arango-Pi{\~n}eros, Sameera Vemulapalli

item.title: Unit Lattices of Totally Complex, non-CM $D_4$-Octic Number Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.31723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a number field, we can endow the unit group of its ring of integers, modulo torsion, with the structure of a lattice. Included in the study of the distributions of these lattices is the classification of shapes of unit lattices arising from $D_4$-quartic number fields with signature $(2,1)$. We extend this work to rank 3, by investigating the shapes of lattices arising from the unit groups of totally complex, non-CM $D_4$-octic number fields. In particular, we show all such unit lattices have automorphism group $D_4\times \mathbb{Z}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$, yet none correspond to Gram matrices whose entries are all algebraic.
item.dc:creator: Sara Chari, Kelly O'Connor

item.title: Mixed moment of twisted modular $L$-functions and Dirichlet $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.31886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a Hecke holomorphic cusp form for $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$. Let $q=p^\gamma$ be a prime power, where $p$ is an arbitrary prime and $\gamma \geq 2$. We establish an asymptotic formula for the mixed moment of $L(s,f\otimes\chi)$ and $L(s,\chi)$ on the central point. We also establish an upper bound for the smoothed sum of Hecke eigenvalues twisted by hyper-Kloosterman sums modulo powers of $2$.
item.dc:creator: Zhaoyan Chen

item.title: Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function on the Critical Line via Bombieri and Murty-Zaharescu
item.description: arXiv:2611.31915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a new proof that the Montgomery--Taylor constant is a lower bound for the proportion of zeros of the Riemann zeta function, or of any fixed Dirichlet \(L\)-function, that are simple and on the critical line. The proof is based on the papers of Bombieri and Murty--Zaharescu.
item.dc:creator: Zimeng Ye

item.title: Eisenstein Cohomology and Critical Values of Certain \(L\)-Functions: A Root-Theoretic Combinatorial Lemma
item.description: arXiv:2611.31920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper gives a root-theoretic extension of the Harder--Raghuram combinatorial lemma, relating criticality of adjacent $L-$values to degrees in nilradical cohomology, to maximal parabolics $P=MU$ of connected split reductive groups with irreducible, essentially tempered cohomological inducing data. At real places, the paper classifies the maximal parabolics for which the two Kostant degrees in the boundary comparison can agree at a regular shift. For each such parabolic, an admissible shift makes both adjacent arguments critical in every Langlands--Shahidi grade exactly when both Kostant degrees equal $\dim U/2$. The classification recovers the two-block parabolics of type $A$ with even product of block sizes (Harder--Raghuram, proved by Weselmann) and the isotropic-line parabolic of type $D_{2m+1}$ for $m\ge2$ (Bhagwat--Raghuram). The only exceptional cases are $P_1$ and $P_6$ of type $E_6$. In all other cases, roots of $U$ fixed by the longest Levi Weyl element confine simultaneous criticality to a singular wall, generalizing the odd-block obstruction for $\mathrm{GL}_N$. Their number is the difference of the fundamental ranks of $M$ and $G$. When the Kostant degrees differ, as in Harder's $\mathrm{GL}_2$ setting, the paper determines which boundary degrees can still coincide. At a complex place, an admissible shift is simultaneously critical exactly when the two conjugate Levi weights after the shift occur in Kostant degrees summing to $\dim U$. With a common relative center, total degree balance at a regular admissible shift characterizes simultaneous criticality at every archimedean place. For split $E_6$ over $\mathbb Q$, a half-spin family yields Eisenstein cohomology classes in degrees $20$ and $21$, including a degree-$20$ class with nonzero restrictions to both associate boundary face types.
item.dc:creator: Farid Hosseinijafari

item.title: $\ell$-abundant numbers and extremal divisor sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.32068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an integer $\ell \ge 1$, we study the sum $\sigma_{(\ell)}(n)$ of the divisors of $n$ whose positive prime exponents are at least $\ell$. The associated abundant, perfect, superabundant, and colossally abundant numbers recover the classical notions when $\ell=1$. We prove strict nesting and infinitude of the abundant classes and derive obstructions to perfection. Our results extend classical work of Ramanujan, Alaoglu, and Erd\H{o}s on superabundant prime-factor structure and colossally abundant exponent selection. For $\ell \ge 2$, we characterize all maximizers of \[ \frac{\sigma_{(\ell)}(n)}{n^{1+\varepsilon}} \] for every $\varepsilon>0$. An explicit logarithmic formula determines the optimal positive exponents, while comparison with exponent $0$ resolves prime entry and all ties. This characterization also yields infinitely many $\ell$-colossally abundant numbers.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Gaber

item.title: Gaps between zeros of Epstein zeta-functions of binary quadratic forms on the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2611.32154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every integral binary quadratic form $Q$ whose discriminant is, up to sign, not a perfect square, the Epstein zeta-function of $Q$ has a zero $\frac12+i\gamma$ with $|\gamma-T|\le T^{2/5+\epsilon}$ for all large $T$. For indefinite $Q$, that is, for zeta-functions of ideal classes of real quadratic orders, this is the first exponent below the classical barrier $1/2$. For positive definite $Q$ it improves the exponents $5/11$ of Jutila and Srinivas and $3/7$ of the authors, and for discriminant $-4m^2$ with $m$ odd we obtain $1/3$. A main ingredient, of independent interest, is an explicit Voronoi summation formula with additive twists to every modulus for the representation numbers of an indefinite binary form. The resulting dual sums are treated by a two-dimensional Weyl differencing, controlled by an exact formula for the Hessian determinant of the differenced phase.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Baier, Srinivas Kotyada, Usha Keshav Sangale

item.title: Poisson Statistics for Values of Binary Quadratic Forms in Short Intervals
item.description: arXiv:2611.32160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the number of integers represented by a binary quadratic form in short intervals. Extending the work of Freiberg, Kurlberg, and Rosenzweig on sums of two squares, we formulate an analogue of the Hardy--Littlewood prime $k$-tuple conjecture for the integers represented by a genus of primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms of a fixed negative discriminant. We show that this hypothesis implies that the number of integers represented by a genus, and by each class in the genus, in a random interval $(n,n+y]$ with $n\le x$, where $y$ is $\tau$ times the average spacing $\sqrt{\log x}/b(d)$, is asymptotically Poisson distributed with parameter $\tau$. The proof uses the method of moments, with Bernays' asymptotic for the number of represented integers in place of the prime number theorem, and an adaptation of Ford's simplified argument for the average of the singular series. We also give numerical evidence for the hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Jack Heimrath

item.title: The first moment of symmetric cube $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a power saving asymptotic formula for the first moment of symmetric cube central $L$-values over Hecke--Maass forms in short spectral windows. As applications, we prove quantitative non-vanishing, an almost-all Lindel\"of bound, and almost-all decay of cubic periods. We also prove the corresponding first moment asymptotic for central derivatives in the holomorphic weight aspect. Our proof begins with an application of the Kuznetsov formula, followed by a first Poisson summation and stationary phase analysis. The key observation is that a periodic cubic factor can be separated from the resulting oscillation and incorporated into the arithmetic sum, allowing a second application of Poisson summation to yield further cancellation.
item.dc:creator: Bingrong Huang, Anders S\"odergren

item.title: The pair correlation of $\alpha n+\beta\log n$ modulo one
item.description: arXiv:2611.32367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that for any non-Liouville irrational $\alpha$ and for any real $\beta\ne0$, the sequence $\left(\alpha n+\beta\log n\right)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ has Poissonian pair correlation modulo one.
item.dc:creator: Nadav Yesha

item.title: A direct majorant and an improved Huber constant on cofinite Fuchsian groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.32398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To obtain an effective upper bound for Huber's constant on cofinite Fuchsian groups, we introduce an algorithm that bypasses the quantitative Karamata Tauberian theorem in estimating spectral-counting growth by direct use of re-optimized Gaussian kernel instead. Further steps involve the different choice of a compactly supported test function, keeping linear and constant terms in the spectral estimate, optimizing the exact cusp geometry, and retaining the full explicit primitive-geodesic majorant in subsequent Chebyshev estimates. The more direct path is established to control the difference between the size of the hyperbolic term in the Selberg trace formula and the second Chebyshev function. Finally, the self-improvement device combined with a knowledge of low-lying spectral data leads to the sharpening that in the case of $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ reads $C_{\mathrm{Hub},\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z}) }<199$. The improvement factor is greater than $8.3\cdot10^{10}$ compared to what was claimed by the initial algorithm and greater than $1.1\cdot10^6$ compared to the currently known bound.
item.dc:creator: Muharem Avdispahi\'{c}

item.title: Integral Means of Fibonacci Numbers: Divisibility, Density, and Arithmetic Structure
item.description: arXiv:2611.32519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by recent works of Fatehizadeh, Yaqubi, Flynn-Connolly, Luca and Marques on the arithmetic mean of Fibonacci numbers, we study divisibility properties of sums of Fibonacci numbers whose indices form arithmetic progressions. We show that infinitely many even and odd $n$ divide such sums, and also the corresponding sums of squares and cubes, and we find all $n$ for which the geometric and harmonic means of $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ are integers. Further, we study the set $\mathcal{A}$ of integers $n\geq2$ for which the arithmetic mean of $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ is an integer. We show that $\mathcal{A}$ is both rich and sparse: it contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions and does not contain odd prime powers, yet $\#\{n\leq x: n\in\mathcal{A}\}\ll x/\sqrt{\log x}$. This density-zero bound holds more generally for every set $\{n: n\mid\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}F_{r+id}\}$. We also establish necessary conditions for three consecutive integral means (a question of Luca and Marques).
item.dc:creator: Sagar Mandal, Mohan

item.title: The centre of mass of the primes and a reflection of Chebyshev's bias
item.description: arXiv:2611.32537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $x\ge2$ we place a unit mass at $\log p$ for each prime $p\le x$, and let $D(x)$ be the distance from the centre of mass of this system to $\log x$; thus $D(p_n)=\log(p_n/G_n)$, where $G_n$ is the geometric mean of the first $n$ primes. Let $D_0(x)$ be the distance obtained when $\pi$ is replaced by $\mathrm{Li}(x)=\int_2^x dt/\log t$. We prove that $D(x)-D_0(x)\ll x^{\Theta-1+\varepsilon}$, where $\Theta$ is the supremum of the real parts of the zeros of $\zeta(s)$, and that the exponent cannot be lowered; in particular, the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to $\log(p_n/G_n)=D_0(p_n)+O_\varepsilon(p_n^{-1/2+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. Under the Riemann hypothesis we prove a pointwise mirror theorem: for large $x$ the centre of mass lies to the left of its predicted position only when $\pi(x)<\mathrm{li}(x)-1.95\sqrt{x}/\log x$. Under the Riemann hypothesis and the linear independence hypothesis, the set of such $x$ has the same logarithmic density as the set on which $\pi(x)>\mathrm{li}(x)$, although for large $x$ the two sets are disjoint. We prove analogues for primes in arithmetic progressions, for the higher moments of the system, and, under a linear independence hypothesis, for $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$, where the biases of even and odd degrees are interchanged.
item.dc:creator: Elham Mehdi-Nezhad, Amir M. Rahimi

item.title: How to facet a gemstone: from potential modularity to modularity lifting
item.description: arXiv:2611.32569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a totally real field and $p\ge7$ a prime unramified in $F$. We prove that a potentially modular $p$-adic representation of $G_F$ which is potentially crystalline with distinct Hodge--Tate weights above $p$, and whose reduction is modular, non-dihedral and satisfies the usual Taylor--Wiles hypothesis, is modular. This removes the hypotheses of [MF] on the Serre weights: the multiplicity-free hypothesis, and the exclusion of Steinberg weights. The same method applies to potentially semistable representations. The proof combines the identity of cycles of [MF] with the modularity of lifts whose local components are mixed along an extension in which $p$ splits. These lifts exist by a theorem of Emerton, Gee, Pan and Zhu, they are potentially automorphic by a theorem of Calegari, Emerton and Gee, and their modularity is proved by tensoring with lifts of an auxiliary residual representation of a different weight: the tensor products lie on a common component of a local deformation ring for $\GL_4$, a lifting theorem of Thorne applies, and the factors of an automorphic tensor product are modular by [Die26].
item.dc:creator: Luis Dieulefait

item.title: Arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas for unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori levels
item.description: arXiv:2611.32570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we formulate conjectural formulas for the arithmetic intersection numbers of special cycles on unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori level structure. We first introduce a framework for formulating Kudla-Rapoport conjectures: we develop the theory of weighted representation densities and special cycles for general parahoric level structures, prove dimension-reduction formulas on both the analytic and geometric sides and duality relations for special cycles. We then formulate the Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for Iwahori level structures based on these properties. Finally, we prove the conjecture when $n=2$.
item.dc:creator: Sungyoon Cho, Qiao He, Chul-hee Lee, Zhiyu Zhang

item.title: On optimal packing of Minkowski spheres
item.description: arXiv:2611.32626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A method has been developed for the optimal packing of a continuum family of one-dimensional Minkowski spheres in the real plane. By applying this method to the problem of packing one-dimensional Minkowski spheres in the plane, an optimal lattice packing for a continuum family of such spheres has been obtained for the first time. Expressions for these optimal packing lattices have been derived, and their validity has been proven. Formulas for the packing density corresponding to these lattices have also been obtained.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Glazunov M. On optimal packing of Minkowski spheres, Cybernetics and systems analysis, vol 61, 192--196, Springer, (2025)
item.dc:creator: Nikolaj M. Glazunov

item.title: Average density of rational points on quartic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.32640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an average asymptotic for the number of rational points of bounded height $B$ on quartic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^3$ of height bounded by $A$, refining an argument of Le Boudec and using techniques of Browning-Le Boudec-Sawin. We extend the range of the asymptotic from $B=o(A)$ to $B=O(A^2)$. As an application, we show that almost all quartic surfaces of height $H$ have no rational point of height $o(H^{5/2})$.
item.dc:creator: Anna Zanoli

item.title: Dobrowolski-type lower bounds for canonical heights of polynomials of Frobenius type
item.description: arXiv:2611.32713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and let $f\in\OK[x]$ be a monic polynomial of degree $d=p^r$ with $f\equiv x^d+c\pmod p$, such as $x^2+c$. We prove that every $\alpha\in\Kbar$ of degree $D$ over $K$ with infinite orbit under $f$ satisfies $$\hh_f(\alpha)\ \ge\ \frac{c_1}{D\log3D}\exp\bigl(-c_2\sqrt{\log3D}\bigr),$$ where $c_1,c_2>0$ depend only on $f$ and $K$. This implies $\hh_f(\alpha)\ge D^{-1-o(1)}$, making progress towards the dynamical Lehmer conjecture. The polynomial $f$ need not be postcritically finite. For such polynomials, for instance $x^2+1$, no lower bound of polynomial decay in $D$ was previously known. For postcritically finite polynomials such as $x^2-1$, it improves the recent quadratic bound of Habegger and Schmidt. The method is motivated by Dobrowolski's proof on Lehmer's problem.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Mello

item.title: An elliptic Lehmer bound of exponent one at a supersingular prime
item.description: arXiv:2611.32749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$ with good supersingular reduction at a prime $\p$. We prove that the N\'eron--Tate height of every non-torsion $P\in E(\Kbar)$ satisfies $\hh_E(P)\ge c\,D^{-1}(\log3D)^{-1}\exp(-c'\sqrt{\log3D})$, where $D=[K(x(P)):K]$ and $c,c'>0$ depend only on $E$, $K$ and $\p$; so $\hh_E(P)\ge D^{-1-o(1)}$. By a result of Elkies this applies to every elliptic curve over $\QQ$, and it improves the exponents of Masser and of Hindry and Silverman.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Mello

item.title: A $2$-adic Kida-type formula for chromatic Selmer groups of elliptic curves and applications to quadratic twists
item.description: arXiv:2611.32770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ with good supersingular reduction at $2$. We study the chromatic ($\sharp/\flat$) Selmer groups of $E$ over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, defined using Sprung's chromatic Coleman maps. We show that at least one of these Selmer groups is $\Lambda$-cotorsion and, assuming the vanishing of the corresponding $\mu$-invariant, establish a $2$-adic Kida-type formula describing the change in the Iwasawa $\lambda$-invariants under base change from $\mathbb{Q}$ to a real quadratic field $F$ in which $2$ is unramified. When $E$ has square-free conductor, applying this formula to $E$ and its quadratic twist $E^D$ yields an explicit formula describing the variation of the chromatic $\lambda$-invariants under twists by positive square-free integers $D\equiv1\pmod4$. As an application, under suitable hypotheses on the root number and chromatic Iwasawa invariants of $E$, we construct explicit sets of primes $\ell$ such that the $2^{\infty}$-Selmer group of $E^{\ell}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ has $\mathbb{Z}_2$-corank one, and determine their positive natural densities.
item.dc:creator: Taiga Adachi

item.title: The integer group determinants for the abelian groups of order 27
item.description: arXiv:2611.32806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We completely determine the integer group determinants for $\mathbb Z_3 \times \mathbb Z_9$ by resolving the allowable multiples of $3$. This completes the Taussky-Todd integer group determinant problem for the abelian groups of order $27$.
item.dc:creator: Michael J. Mossinghoff, Chris Pinner

item.title: On the Fujii conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2611.32862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the Riemann hypothesis for the nonprincipal character modulo four, we disprove Fujii's first conjecture on exponential weights and prove his second conjecture on iterated weights by Mellin convolution [Proc. Japan Acad. Ser. A Math. Sci. 64 (1988), 260--263]. Further, we unify the two conjectures through a two-parameter family of Mellin kernels and prove that the prime race exhibits a phase transition.
item.dc:creator: Ziyu Neroli

item.title: On Waring's problem for fourth powers
item.description: arXiv:2611.32904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every sufficiently large integer $n$, satisfying $n\equiv 1,2,3,\dots,11\pmod*{16}$, can be written as a sum of $11$ biquadrates. In particular, $G^{\#}(4)\leq 11$. This improves upon $G^{\#}(4)\leq 12$ due to Vaughan in 1989.
item.dc:creator: Xuanzhe Wang, Lilu Zhao

item.title: From hockey stick to boomerang via Appell polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.32926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Pascal's triangle, the hockey-stick identities are well known as certain sums over the binomial coefficients, e.g., lying in a fixed row or column of the triangle. We establish unified identities that are connected with Appell polynomials, from which the hockey-stick identities follow as a very special case. Subsequently, we derive several identities for (reciprocal) Appell polynomials yielding applications to the Bernoulli and Euler polynomials. As a result, we obtain new identities for the Bernoulli, Euler, Fibonacci, and Genocchi numbers, as well as, power sums. This also leads to infinitely many recurrence relations for these numbers.
item.dc:creator: Bernd C. Kellner

item.title: Boomerang identities and binomial transform
item.description: arXiv:2611.32965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Pascal's triangle, the boomerang identities, which were recently introduced, combine and extend the well-known hockey-stick identities of the binomial coefficients by allowing additional terms. We show that the binomial transform of sequences in a ring play a central role in this context. Subsequently, we show several applications to Bell and Bernoulli numbers and polynomials, Appell polynomials, as well as, to harmonic, Fibonacci, Lucas, and Stirling numbers.
item.dc:creator: Bernd C. Kellner

item.title: The local Weil explicit formula and related structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.33001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces constructed from the local Weil quadratic form associated with the Riemann zeta function. Wherever this form is positive definite, we prove a local explicit formula expressing the Weil distribution in terms of the discrete spectra of self-adjoint extensions of the differentiation operator. We characterize the Riemann hypothesis by the uniform boundedness of the diagonal values of the reproducing kernels. We then study the chain of de Branges spaces and recover the Hamiltonian of the corresponding canonical system explicitly from these kernels under local positivity, without assuming the Riemann hypothesis. Finally, assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we study the asymptotic behavior of solutions of this system.
item.dc:creator: Masatoshi Suzuki

item.title: Perfect powers with small exponents from products of terms in progression
item.description: arXiv:2611.33008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be a large integer, and let $\ell$ be an integer with $2 \leq \ell \leq (\log \log k)^{1/5}$. We determine all solutions to the Diophantine equation \begin{align*} n(n+d)\cdots (n+(k-1)d)=y^\ell \end{align*} in nonzero integers $n,d,y$ with $d\geq 1$ and $\text{gcd}(n,d)=1$. We also prove results for generalizations where the product $n(n+d)\cdots (n+(k-1)d)$ is ``almost'' a perfect power, rather than exactly a perfect power, and where some of the terms $n+id$ are dropped from the product.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Pratt

item.title: Prismatic construction of crystalline deformation rings up to p-power torsion
item.description: arXiv:2611.33029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the deformation of Galois representations which are etale realizations of finitely generated prismatic F-crystals and show the deformation functor is pro-represented by a complete Noetherian local ring whose Z_p-flat quotient coincides with Kisin's crystalline deformation ring. As a consequence, we obtain a universal prismatic F-crystal with coefficients in Kisin's crystalline deformation ring.
item.dc:creator: Yu Min

item.title: Properties of the Sawin--Wood Model for Unramified Galois Groups of Global Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.33073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove almost-sure finite generation and finite presentation in the pro-$|\Gamma|'$ $\Gamma$-category for the Sawin--Wood measure $\nu_{\Gamma,n,U}$, where $\Gamma$ is a non-trivial finite group, $n$ is coprime to $|\Gamma|$, and $U$ is a nonempty multiset of conjugacy classes of $\Gamma$. The $\Gamma$-generator rank of the random group $X$ has the sharp tail $\mathbf{P}(d_\Gamma(X) \geq r) = Ce^{-\kappa r^2-\zeta r}(1+O(e^{-\varepsilon r}))$, where $C>0$, $\kappa>0$, and $\zeta\in\mathbb{R}$ are explicit constants depending on $n$, $\Gamma$ and $U$, and $\varepsilon>0$. Almost surely, $X$ admits a presentation with the minimum number of $\Gamma$-generators, using at most $|U|$ more defining $\Gamma$-relations than generators. We also prove that every open subgroup of $X$ has finite abelianization almost surely under the assumption that for every complex representation of $\Gamma$ there is an element in $U$ that fixes a nonzero vector. Finally, we prove that $H_2(X,\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})=0$ almost surely when $n=1$, $\Gamma$ is cyclic, and $U$ contains only the conjugacy class of a generator of $\Gamma$ (with multiplicity one).
item.dc:creator: Mark Shusterman, Gonen Zimmerman

item.title: Forms and polynomial covers in many variables
item.description: arXiv:2611.33114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a homogeneous form of degree $d \ge 2$, and let $\sigma$ be the affine dimension of the singular locus of $F = 0$. We prove that the hypersurface $F = 0$ satisfies the smooth Hasse principle whenever \[ n - \sigma \ge 2^{d + 1} - 3. \] This is the first improvement in the order of magnitude of Birch's classical result. We also apply the method to the counting problem for polynomial covers $F(x_1,\ldots,x_n) = g(y)$, and give a condition on $n - \sigma$ under which Serre's conjectural upper bound holds and another condition under which the expected asymptotic formula holds.
item.dc:creator: Yijie Diao, Lena Wurzinger

item.title: Progress on the Stable Fields Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.31356v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every infinite stable field of positive characteristic is separably closed. We also show that the field $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property (hence is unstable).
item.dc:creator: G Conant, J Freitag, C Terry

item.title: Supercuspidal representations and types via double covers and the Fourier--Weil representation
item.description: arXiv:2611.31396v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a construction of supercuspidal representations and types for tame $p$-adic groups whose input is a generic essentially depth-zero representation of a double covers of twisted Levi subgroups. This clarifies and simplifies existing constructions by automatically producing and explaining the twisting quadratic character of Fintzen--Kaletha--Spice, the roots of unity in the Harish-Chandra character formula, and making the connection to the Galois side of the local Langlands correspondence immediate. The main innovation is the use of a Fourier model of the Weil representation defined on an extension of the symplectic group by the Witt group.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Fintzen, Tasho Kaletha

item.title: Symbolic Proof Compression and Fractal Universality: A Conditional Non-Constructive Refutation of the Riemann Hypothesis
item.description: arXiv:2611.31469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building on S.~C.~Woon's (1994) fractal and symbolic reformulation of Voronin's Universality Theorem, we construct a formal, non-constructive proof-by-contradiction architecture exploring the Riemann Hypothesis ($\mathsf{RH}$). Woon's Corollary~3 permits arbitrary finite binary strings to be encoded into nowhere-vanishing exponential waveforms on a closed disk inside the critical strip. Combining effective upper bounds for Voronin universality (Good, Garunk\v{s}tis) with Cauchy-integral Taylor decoding yields an explicit finite rational grid $\mathcal{G}_{L_0}$ below an effective ceiling $H_{\mathrm{crit}}(L_0)$ within which every formal proof of bit-length at most $L_0$ is imprinted with zero flipped digits. We introduce a conjectural \emph{Zeta-Universal Symbolic Proof Compression Hypothesis} ($\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$), positing that the global regularity implied by $\mathsf{RH}$ compresses true $\Pi_1^0$ statements about $\zeta(s)$ into $\mathsf{ZFC}$ derivations of bounded length $L_0$. Assuming classical logic and $\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$, G\"odel--Carnap diagonalization over bounded zeta-encoded provability yields a contradiction. The self-referential result converts a digital encoding framework with any uniform proof-compression principle for RH into an immediate non-constructive refutation of RH. Given that, with human input and computer assistance, $\mathsf{RH}$ has been formally verified in the Lean theorem prover strictly within constructive logic, this contradiction does not refute $\mathsf{RH}$. Instead, it falsifies $\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$. We conclude by isolating the exact proof-theoretic obstruction---Pudl\'ak's lower bound on bounded reflection proofs---showing why the analytic regularity of $\mathsf{RH}$ cannot compress logical self-reference, and exposing the limits of applying the Law of Excluded Middle to uncomputably bounded searches.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Martin Lisewski

item.title: On the unirationality of anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces: the infinite families
item.description: arXiv:2611.31552v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces fall into finitely many sporadic families and four infinite families. We prove that the anticanonical surfaces lying in the infinite families are unirational over their field of definition. Over a Hilbertian field, we further prove that a Hilbert subset of members consists of nonrational surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Giulia Gugiatti, Alex Massarenti

item.title: The local intertwining relation for inner forms of $\mathrm{GL}_N$
item.description: arXiv:2611.31683v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The local intertwining relation for inner forms of general linear groups over a local field asserts that the normalized intertwining operator for every parabolically induced representation arising from a local A-parameter is the identity operator. Our main theorem verifies the claim over local fields of characteristic zero. This will serve as a vital ingredient for completing the local intertwining relation and endoscopic classification for non-quasi-split unitary groups.
item.dc:creator: Hiraku Atobe, Tasho Kaletha, Alberto Minguez, Sug Woo Shin

item.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties II. Fibrations over a polarized base
item.description: arXiv:2611.31691v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the height and energy inequalities for fibrations over curves to a fibration $f:X\to Y$ over a polarized variety $(Y,B)$. For an integrable relatively nef adelic line bundle $\bar L$, we prove a height inequality under the assumption that $L$ is nef on the inverse image of a geometric generic complete-intersection curve in $Y$. We deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model when $L$ is $f$-ample. For a slope semistable bundle on a fixed polarized complex variety, we show that the infimum of the energy on its projective bundle equals the infimum of Donaldson's functional on Hermitian quotient metrics, with the normalization given below.
item.dc:creator: Shou-Wu Zhang

item.title: The Lafforgue Transform
item.description: arXiv:2611.32627v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this report, we survey the \emph{Lafforgue transform}, a natural representation-theoretic map from the Kazhdan cocenter to the Bernstein center of a reductive group over a local field. Its motivation comes from our study of the Braverman-Kazhdan proposal, a conjectural framework for establishing the meromorphic continuation and functional equations of general automorphic $L$-functions through harmonic analysis on possibly singular varieties. For $G=\SL_2$ and $\GL_2$, we explain how the stable part of the Lafforgue transform and its distinguished section are realized as integral transforms on the Steinberg-Hitchin base, with formulas of motivic nature that are valid over every local field.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of the International Consortium of Chinese Mathematicians, 2026
item.dc:creator: Zhilin Luo

item.title: A Barsotti-Weil isomorphism for Taelman units
item.description: arXiv:2611.32767v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The positive-characteristic analogue of motivic cohomology with coefficients in an Anderson A-motive M over a function field of transcendence degree one was introduced in an earlier work of the author. In this paper, we prove that, when M arises as the dual of the A-motive of an Anderson module E that is abelian, uniformizable, and has everywhere good reduction, the corresponding A-motivic cohomology coincides with the module of Taelman units of E, up to a twist by the module of K\"ahler differentials of A. To this end, we recast the theory of Anderson generating functions in the spirit of earlier work of Maurischat and the author on special functions.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Gazda

item.title: On Presburger Arithmetic Expanded with Prime Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.32977v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove unconditionally that the first-order theory of Presburger arithmetic expanded by a predicate for the primes is undecidable. Bateman, Jockusch and Woods proved this in 1993 assuming Dickson's conjecture. We use the counter-machine framework of Karimov, Nieuwveld and Ouaknine and their idea of using `arbitrary permutations', and the number-theoretic input comes from Hildebrand and Maier's 1988 proof that the limit points of $k$ consecutive normalised prime gaps have positive measure. We use a discrete version, which they obtain before limits are taken. The key lemma is that although Hildebrand and Maier's result does not seem to give arbitrary permutations of consecutive prime gaps, it gives arbitrary permutations for the differences $p_i - q_i$ for two finite blocks of consecutive primes $p_0 < \cdots < p_k$ and $q_0 < \cdots < q_k$. Moreover, with the same key lemma, we show that Presburger arithmetic expanded with the function that maps $n$ to the $n$th prime defines multiplication.
item.dc:creator: Joris Nieuwveld

item.title: Undershoot of h-fold sumsets: Ap\'ery spectra, similar ordering and the three-distance theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.33046v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a finite set $A_0\subset\mathbb{N}$ with $0\in A_0$, $\max A_0=d$ and $\gcd(A_0)=1$, and a target $T$, the undershoot at level $h$ is the distance from $T$ down to the largest element of the $h$-fold sumset $hA_0$ not above $T$. Its total over $T\in[0,hd]$ is bounded in $h$: for large $h$ it equals the sum of the masses of two numerical semigroups attached to $A_0$, where the mass adds $L(L+1)/2$ over the maximal runs of $L$ gaps. We describe how the total reaches this limit: it can rise to it, fall to it, or climb past it and return. When the monomial curve of $A_0$ is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, two Ap\'ery sets give every undershoot exactly, and partial sums of a fixed spectrum bound the total from below, with equality at every level exactly when two threshold sequences are similarly ordered; the total then rises concavely to its limit, reached exactly at the sumsets regularity. We characterize the similarly ordered four-element sets. For $\{0,a,b,2b\}$ with $0<a<b$ coprime, the three-distance theorem gives the total in explicit quadratic pieces. A non-Cohen-Macaulay set exceeds its limit at every failing level $h$ with $hd$ at least the sum of the two conductors; every such four-element set does so, and a five-element example never does. For arbitrary sets, finite corner data give the exact undershoot over any window.
item.dc:creator: Prashant Chaudhary, Kapil Khandelwal

item.title: Brauer classes of representations of division algebras and their Langlands parameters
item.description: arXiv:2611.33116v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every depth-zero supercuspidal representation $\pi$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ with algebraic-valued central character, we prove that the Brauer obstructions to realizing its Jacquet-Langlands transfer and its normalized Langlands parameter $\varphi_\pi\otimes|\cdot|^{-(n-1)/2}$ over their common field of rationality $E=\mathbb{Q}(\pi)$ sum to $(n-1)[B_{p,\infty}\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} E]$. Here $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ is finite, the transfer is to the units of the central division algebra over $K$ of invariant $1/n$, and $B_{p,\infty}$ is the quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$ ramified exactly at $p$ and $\infty$. We conjecture this identity without the depth restriction. For arbitrarily large $n=p-1$, we construct simple supercuspidal representations satisfying the same sum formula. Their transfers have finite-order central character and Schur index $n$, whereas their normalized parameters have index $n/2$. Since these transfers are not self-dual, the unequal indices contradict the isomorphism of Schur algebras conjectured by Prasad and Ramakrishnan.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Xu

item.title: Extending van der Geer and Hirzebruch's generalization of Construction A
item.description: arXiv:2502.19753v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper discusses a generalization of Construction A and its application to root lattices of type $A_n, D_n,$ and $E_n$. While the classical Construction A provides a correspondence between binary codes and lattices, and its extension to cyclotomic fields relates $p$-ary codes to lattices over the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$, we further extend this framework to a broader class of even root lattices. Specifically, for a given lattice $\Lambda$ of type $A_n, D_n,$ or $E_n$, we define a surjective mapping $\rho$ from the dual lattice $\Lambda^*$ to a finite ring $R$ isomorphic to the quotient $\Lambda^*/\Lambda$. We then characterize the conditions under which the resulting lattice $(\rho^{\oplus m})^{-1}(C)$, constructed from an $R$-code $C$ of length $m$, becomes an even unimodular lattice. Furthermore, we apply our generalized Construction A to the algebraic lattices of type $D_4$ and $E_6$ realized as fractional ideals of cyclotomic fields. Consequently, we show that the theta functions associated with these lattices can be expressed via the weight enumerators of the corresponding codes, proving that they are Hilbert modular forms over totally real fields.
item.dc:creator: Riku Higa

item.title: A full-rank subgroup of Bloch Groups of CM Fields
item.description: arXiv:2507.05792v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article generalizes the result of Burns et al (2022), to find an algorithm to find some elements generating a full-rank subgroup of the torsion-free part of Bloch group of a certain CM number field, and compute the rank of it.
item.dc:creator: Wenhuan Huang

item.title: Iwasawa Theory of Elliptic Curves in Quadratic Twist Families
item.description: arXiv:2507.21339v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we use two different approaches -- one algebraic and the other analytic -- to study the variation of Iwasawa invariants of rational elliptic curves in some quadratic twist families. The analytic approach involves a thorough investigation of half-integral weight modular forms. On the other hand, the algebraic proof requires studying the BDP-Selmer groups and the fine Selmer groups.
item.dc:creator: Debanjana Kundu, Katharina M\"uller

item.title: On moments of the Erd\H{o}s--Hooley Delta-function
item.description: arXiv:2512.05652v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For integer $n\geqslant 1$ and real $u$, let $\Delta(n,u):=|\{d:d\mid n,\,{\rm e}^u<d\leqslant {\rm e}^{u+1}\}|$. The Erd\H{o}s--Hooley Delta-function is then defined by $\Delta(n):=\max_{u\in{\mathbb R}}\Delta(n,u).$ We provide new upper bounds for weighted real moments of this function.
item.dc:creator: R. de la Bret\`eche, G. Tenenbaum

item.title: Unlikely intersections with CM abelian varieties in a family and explicit bounds for canonical heights under endomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2601.05919v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{A} \rightarrow S$ be a non-isotrivial abelian scheme over a smooth irreducible curve and let $\mathcal{C} \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ be an irreducible curve, all defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$. In 2020, Barroero and Capuano proved that, if $\mathcal{C}$ is not contained in a proper subgroup scheme, then its intersection with the union of the flat subgroup schemes of $\mathcal{A}$ of codimension at least $2$ is finite. We complement this result by proving that, if $\mathcal{C}$ is contained neither in a fixed fiber nor in a proper flat subgroup scheme, even after a finite base change, then only finitely many points of $\mathcal{C}$ lie in a proper algebraic subgroup of a CM fiber of $\mathcal{A}$. This generalizes a previous result of Barroero for fibered powers of elliptic schemes. A key ingredient of the proof is an explicit control of canonical heights under endomorphisms: for an abelian variety $A/\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, an ample symmetric divisor $D$ and $f \in \mathrm{End}(A)$, we bound $\widehat{h}_{A,D}(f(P))$ from above and from below in terms of $\widehat{h}_{A,D}(P)$, with optimal constants given by the largest and the smallest eigenvalue of $f^{\dagger}f$, where $^{\dagger}$ is the Rosati involution associated with $D$.
item.dc:creator: Luca Ferrigno

item.title: The Subtractive Divisor Orbit: Unconditional Bounds, Parity Constraints, and a Conditional Framework
item.description: arXiv:2604.25446v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $a(n)$ be the number of iterations of $F(m)=m-\tau(m)$ needed to reach zero, where $\tau(m)$ counts the positive divisors of $m$. Write $\Delta(n)=a(n)-a(n-1)$. We prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $X$, each of the inequalities $\Delta(n)\ge X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ and $\Delta(n)\le -X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ holds for at least $X^{1-\varepsilon}$ integers $1\le n\le X$. The proof uses the identity $F(2m)=2F(m)$ at odd $m$ and the fact that an odd orbit first changes parity at a square. For every fixed $C>0$, a positive proportion of starting values $n\in(X,4X]$ satisfy $\left|a(n)-\frac{Cn}{\log n}\right|\gg_C\frac{\sqrt X}{\log X}$. For the hitting time itself we prove $a(x)\ll_b\frac{x}{(\log x)^b}$ for every $b<\log 2$, together with a lower bound having logarithmic exponent $2.988206\ldots$. On complete crossings of $(N,2N]$, with $Z=2N$, the logarithm of the step size has normal order $(\log 2)\log\log Z$, uniformly in the starting value. Computations through $10^9$ give the largest positive and negative first differences in this range.
item.dc:creator: Marco Mantovanelli

item.title: Power-saving density bounds for $K$-point configurations in $\mathbb{Z}^d$
item.description: arXiv:2609.13126v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $d,K,N\in \mathbb{N}$ with $K\geq 3$ and $d\geq 4K+4$. Let $\Delta\subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ be the vertex set of a nondegenerate $(K-1)$-simplex, and let $A\subseteq[N]^d$ contain no nontrivial similar copy of $\Delta$. We prove that \[ |A|\ll_{\Delta,d} N^{d-c_{\Delta,d}}, \] improving upon a polylogarithmic bound due to Magyar. We combine an induction-on-scale argument with the circle method, and we introduce a ``cut operator'' method to decouple the weighted exponential sum over the system of quadratic forms describing the simplex. Our proof combines ideas from graph theory, functional analysis, and the geometry of numbers. In the process, we apply Finner's fractional form of H\"older's inequality, the analytic large sieve, and Kim's mean value formula for primitive lattice flags.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Lott, \'Akos Magyar, Nagendar Reddy Ponagandla

item.title: Every integer greater than 24 is the sum of a prime and a non-square-free integer
item.description: arXiv:2609.14714v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lee and O'Clarey proved that every odd integer $n>24$ can be written as the sum of a prime and a positive integer that is not square-free. Under the generalised Riemann hypothesis, they established the same conclusion for every integer $n>24$. We prove this result unconditionally, confirming their stated expectation. The proof combines an elementary congruence argument, finite computation, and explicit estimates for primes in arithmetic progressions.
item.dc:creator: Peter J. Campbell

item.title: S-squareful values of binary quadratic forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.20316v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Shute showed that the leading constant in the asymptotic formula for squareful values of the form $ax^2+by^2$ does not match with the conjecture established by Pieropan, Smeets, Tanimoto and V\'arilly-Alvarado. In this paper, $S$-squareful values of this form are considered for $S$ the set of primes that divide $a$ and $b$. We prove an asymptotic formula for these numbers and show that the leading constant of the asymptotic formula still does not match the conjecture. Furthermore, we consider the updated conjecture established by Chow, Loughran, Takloo-Bighash, and Tanimoto regarding the leading constant for Campana points in the given setting and show that this constant is consistent with our computed constant.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Sophie Pohl

item.title: On a conjecture of Velani
item.description: arXiv:2610.28839v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the approximation of elements of the middle-third Cantor set by dyadic rationals, and natural extensions. We prove a conjecture of Velani, completing the metric theory for the Cantor measure. Our key method enables a quantitative study of the incommensurability of binary and ternary expansions of integers, initiated by Furstenberg. The method has other applications, e.g. $\sum_{k} |\hat{\mu}(2^k)|^\sigma < \infty$ for any $\sigma > 0$, where $\mu$ is the Cantor measure.
item.dc:creator: Sam Chow, Han Yu

item.title: On Hecke algebras at exceptional Eisenstein primes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35559v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the structure over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of the Hecke algebra acting on ordinary cusp forms in the Eisenstein, non-$p$-distinguished case. Our results and methods draw on four complementary approaches: deformation theory, through $R=\mathbf{T}$ theorems; Iwasawa theory, through connections to Sharifi's conjecture; $p$-adic $L$-functions, through an exceptional zero formula; and computational experiments using Magma. We also obtain new results regarding the Coleman--Greenberg conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Maksoud

item.title: Effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate distribution for Abelian varieties with applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.36464v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we aim to establish a uniform effective form of the Chebotarev-Sato-Tate distribution for abelian varieties with a connected Sato-Tate group, conditional on standard analytic conjectures for L-functions attached to the relevant irreducible representations. This improves on the exponent of Bucur, Fite, and Kedlaya (Theorem 1.1, 2024) whenever the Sato-Tate group has rank greater than one. We also establish a variant for prime-dependent regions of the Sato-Tate group and finite Galois extensions that vary with the counting parameter. As an application, for a normalized non-CM newform f of weight 2 and level N with a quadratic coefficient field, we obtain a conditional upper bound for Pi(x):=|{p<= x: p does not divide N, a(p) is in Q}|, where a(p) is the pth Fourier coefficient of f. In addition, we formulate a discrepancy conjecture that allows us to prove Murty's asymptotic prediction (Conjecture 3.4, 1999) for Pi(x).
item.dc:creator: Mohammed Amin Amri

item.title: Congruence properties modulo powers of 3 for designated summands in partitions into odd parts
item.description: arXiv:2611.15164v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Using $3$-dissection identities and coefficient extraction, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of two infinite families of arithmetic subsequences of $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$. We establish lower bounds for the $3$-adic valuations of the polynomial coefficients, thereby proving two infinite families of congruences conjectured by Lin (J. Number Theory,~2018). We then estimate the $3$-adic valuations of two-by-two determinants formed from consecutive coefficient vectors. These estimates yield two infinite families of internal congruences modulo high powers of $3$. The internal congruences and the initial generating functions also establish the generating-function congruences conjectured by Singh and Barman (Ramanujan J.,~2025).
item.dc:creator: Xingyi Li, Dazhao Tang

item.title: Cyclic Self-Dual Codes over Rings and Unimodular Lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.24153v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an explicit construction of cyclic Euclidean self-dual codes over $\mathbb{Z}/p^{2}\mathbb{Z}$, where $p$ is an odd prime, and use Construction~A to obtain unimodular lattices with large minimum norms. The construction is based on reciprocal factorizations of $x^n-1$. We explicitly describe the associated residue and torsion codes and analyze the relationship between minimum Euclidean weights and lattice minimum norms. We construct a unimodular lattice of minimum norm~$4$ in dimension~$49$, unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$5$ in dimensions $53$, $55$, $58$, $59$, and~$61$, and extremal unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$6$ in dimensions $69$ and~$71$. Using shadow theory and harmonic theta series, we prove that extremal unimodular lattices do not exist in dimensions $59$ and~$61$. Together with the known upper bounds, these results establish the optimality of the constructed lattices in all eight dimensions. In particular, we determine the previously unknown optimal minimum norms of unimodular lattices in five dimensions: $53$, $55$, $61$, $69$, and~$71$. We further construct unimodular lattices whose minimum norms are exactly one below the corresponding extremal bounds in dimensions $62$, $63$, $65$, $67$, $70$, $89$, $91$, $92$, $93$, and~$94$.
item.dc:creator: Minjia Shi, Mengru Yang, Patrick Sol\'e

item.title: Square-root cancellation in three hyperbolic counting problems via maximal estimates
item.description: arXiv:2611.26738v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study three counting problems for lattice orbits in hyperbolic space: counting orbit points within a prescribed distance of a fixed closed geodesic or a totally geodesic hyperplane, and counting orbit points above a prescribed height at a cusp. For almost every base point, we obtain error bounds of square-root size up to logarithmic factors. For the geodesic and hyperplane counts, these bounds match the conjectured exponents and improve earlier results due to Good and Laaksonen. For these two problems, we adapt the method of maximal estimates developed by Chatzakos and Dimakis for hyperbolic lattice counting, formulating it in both a discrete and a continuous framework. For the hyperplane problem, we also obtain an asymptotic formula for the spatial second moment of the error term, involving an almost periodic function. For the cusp problem, the square-root bound can be deduced from work of Yu, which incorporates Schmidt's dyadic maximal argument. We present a proof, together with an $\Omega$-result supporting the optimality of the exponent $1/2$ for at least one cusp of any group that is not essentially cuspidal.
item.dc:creator: Marios Voskou

item.title: Elliptic curves with torsion Z/5Z: exact rank four over Q(k) and rank at least five infinitely often
item.description: arXiv:2611.28977v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give two elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}(k)$ with torsion group $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank exactly $4$, with four explicit independent points. The upper bounds come from reducing the relevant elliptic surfaces modulo suitable primes and are unconditional. They match the known lower bound for the generic rank with this torsion, due to Eroshkin, and are not isomorphic to Eroshkin's curve or to each other: their parametrising maps to $X_1(5)$ have degree $8$ instead of $12$, the constructions are dihedral rather than biquadratic, and their branch loci differ. In each case, two of the points come from a ``doubling'' step in the spirit of Jaswal. Adding one further condition to the second curve, coming from a quadratic twist over an intermediate conic, gives a fifth independent point over a genus-one curve of rank two. Hence there are infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank at least $5$, improving the known bound $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 4$ to $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 5$.
item.dc:creator: Andrej Dujella, Juan Carlos Peral

item.title: Vanishing results for the coherent cohomology of automorphic vector bundles over the Siegel variety in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2202.06691v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove vanishing results for the coherent cohomology of the good reduction modulo $p$ of the Siegel variety with coefficients in some automorphic bundles. We show that for an automorphic bundle with highest weight $\lambda$ near the walls of the anti-dominant Weyl chamber, there is an integer $e \geq 0$ such that the cohomology is concentrated in degrees $[0, e]$. The accessible weights with our method are not necessarily regular and not necessarily $p$-small. Since our method is technical, we also provide an algorithm written in Sage that computes explicitly the vanishing results.
item.dc:creator: Thibault Alexandre

item.title: Lonely Runner Relations
item.description: arXiv:2609.06259v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the \emph{Lonely Runner Conjecture} (LRC), conceived by J\"org M.~Wills in the 1960's: Given positive integers $n_1, n_2, \dots, n_k$, there exists a positive real number $t$ such that for all $1 \le j \le k$ the distance of $t \, n_j$ to the nearest integer is at least $\frac{ 1 }{ k+1 }$. We prove that for any counterexample or tight instance $\mathbf{n}$ of LRC, $\mathbf{m} \cdot \mathbf{n} = 0$ for some $\mathbf{m} \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $0 < \| \mathbf{m} \|_1 \le \min(2k+3, \ \frac{ k+1 }{ k-1 } \mathrm{flt}(k))$ where $\mathrm{flt}(k)$ denotes Khinchin's (1948) \emph{flatness constant} limiting the lattice width of a $k$-dimensional convex body without interior integer points. In other words, potential counterexamples to LRC lie on a finite set of hyperplanes in the parameter space. Our proofs use Fourier analysis and a geometric reformulation of LRC, and our results generalize to the situation of shifted lonely runners of varying measures of loneliness. Our results imply and generalize a theorem of Czerwi\'nski (2012) that when we choose $\mathbf{n}$ at random then, with probability tending to 1, the measure of loneliness $\frac{ 1 }{ k+1 }$ can be replaced by $\frac 1 2 - \epsilon$. We also show that the lattice width of the polyhedra appearing in conjunction with LRC grows linearly with the dimension.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Beck, Samuel Everett

item.title: Transcending Algebraic Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.00335v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give an exposition of some of the ideas leading up to Jacob Tsimerman's groundbreaking work developing the theory of o-minimal definability in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Simpson

item.title: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40551v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As AI's mathematical capabilities rapidly improve, meaningful benchmarks are shifting from university-level problems and math olympiads to research-level mathematics. The Ramanujan Challenge is a benchmark comprised of research-level problems in number theory, including unpublished results and open conjectures. It presented concrete formulas for mathematical constants whose correctness can be checked numerically, while their proofs may require non-obvious mathematics. Here, we analyze the Challenge submissions, measuring the relative success of different AI models, Computer Algebra Systems (CAS), and formal tools. We find correct submissions that are conceptually distinct from the official solutions, and a proof of one of the published open conjectures. Evaluating the submissions exposed a second challenge: judging complex proofs reliably at scale. We introduce an AI-assisted evaluation pipeline for natural language proofs, CAS code, and Lean formalizations that assesses semantic and logical correctness. Compared with the conventional one-shot LLM judgment, our pipeline reduces false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs from 23% to 6% and improves judgment accuracy on supporting code from 46% to 58%. This approach provides a methodology for evaluating research-level mathematics at scale, with potential applications across mathematics and AI for science.
item.dc:creator: Alan Sorani, Ashvni Narayanan, Michael Shalyt, Tali Monderer, Rotem Kalisch, Hila Barkan, Elyasheev Leibtag, Shachar Weinbaum, Carsten Schneider, John Campbell, Ido Kaminer

item.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
item.description: arXiv:2611.24775v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. We disprove this conjecture for every exponent $n=2k$ with $k\ge3$ odd. For each such $n$, we prove that $D(C_n^r)>r(n-1)+1$ for every $r\ge \frac{5n}{2}$. For rank $r=3$, we prove that the equality $D(C_n^3)=3n-2$ holds for all sufficiently large integers $n$.
item.dc:creator: Weidong Gao, Alfred Geroldinger, Guoqing Wang, Xiangneng Zeng
